chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sayf al-Tammarr said: I said to Abu Basir, 'I would like you to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'

About a man who exchanged two qasarat (containers of dates) containing cooked/dried dates for one qasarat containing split dates. He said: So Abu Basir asked him about that, and he said, 'This is disliked (makruh).'

Abu Basir said, 'And why is it disliked?' He said, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) disliked exchanging one wasq of the dates of Medina with two wasqs of the dates of Khaybar, and Ali (peace be upon him) did not dislike the halal (permissible).'

key_terms.تَمْرِ اَلْمَدِينَةِ: Dates of Medina (known for superior quality)
key_terms.وَسْقاً: A specific measure of volume for dry goods

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging different qualities of dates in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that while exchanging unequal quantities of the same commodity (like Medinan vs. Khaybari dates) is permissible (*halal*), it is discouraged (*makruh*) to avoid *gharar* (hidden inequity) and preserve social fairness, as exemplified by Imam Ali’s (AS) practice. It distinguishes between the legal validity of the contract and the recommended prudence in commercial dealings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both juridical correctness and ethical refinement (*adab*) in trade.
